title: Chords and inversions
summary: Build tonic and primary triads, and name chords and their positions.

provenance.notes: Items drawn from the seeded generators with a teaching-point filter, then fixed. Music and answers come from the rule engine; prompts and feedback are original.

items.prompt: Write the tonic triad of F major in the treble clef, in root position, using accidentals.
hints: Chord I is built on degree 1 of the scale: that note, the 3rd above it and the 5th above it.

feedback.correct: Yes: the tonic, the 3rd and the 5th.

mistakes.wrong-degree: Find the root: rearrange the notes into stacked 3rds — the lowest note of that stack is the root.
mistakes.root-confused-with-bass: The lowest note isn't always the root. Stack the notes in 3rds to find it, then check the inversion.
mistakes.inversion-misread: Inversion depends on which note of the triad is in the bass: root (a), 3rd (b) or 5th (c).
mistakes.leading-note-not-raised: In minor keys, chords use the harmonic minor, so the leading note is raised.
mistakes.note-missing: One of the notes doesn't belong. A triad has a root, a 3rd and a 5th.

feedback.fallback: Not quite. Find the root first, then the bass note.

items.prompt: Name this chord in G minor: give its Roman numeral and position (for example, IVb).

Rearrange the notes into a stack of 3rds to find the root, then look at the lowest note for the position.

hints: Put the right note in the bass first.
